reported_packages.relationship: identical checkpoint, views, cache and rows as the bias package; only the fixed uniform prior bias differs (3077 changed predictions)

interpretation.established: The v2 checkpoint is genuinely better before correction (+1.42pp / +533 images raw), but the fixed uniform-prior bias repairs much less on it (+1.71pp / +639) than on the v1 768 checkpoint (+2.88pp / +1077), so after correction the two models are only +0.25pp / +95 images apart.
interpretation.hypothesis: The fixed uniform-prior correction partly absorbs model-quality differences; the corrected score compresses toward roughly 74.4-74.7 for this model family.
interpretation.confound_not_resolved: The two lineages do not share the same multi-view reduction: v1 sums six-view logits (equivalent to a geometric mean of per-view probabilities) while v2 uses log(mean of six-view probabilities), and the fixed 200-iteration damping-1 bias acts in that score space. The gain difference therefore mixes model and decode and cannot be attributed to either alone.
interpretation.consequence_for_80_percent: If a similar pass-through held, closing the remaining 1997 corrected errors by raw-accuracy gains alone would need an implausible raw jump; the remaining errors are content/confusion errors, not prior shift.

next_slot_recommendation: 512 full SWA six-view + fixed bias (Desktop/noise/v1_512_test_bias_control_20261001_512_test_bias_submission.zip): third checkpoint under the same v1 decode protocol, giving a third (raw, bias) point to test whether the bias gain is decode-driven or model-driven

deprioritized: v2 full_576 EMA and RAW3-5 averaging, because the compression pattern above predicts little corrected-score gain per unit of raw gain; they are not withdrawn, only no longer the best use of a slot
